headline: From eMule to MoMA PS1: DJ Marfox and Lisbon's batida
caption:
In 2006, 37 tracks went up on eMule.

That compilation is now seen as the founding release of Lisbon's ghetto sound. It came from DJs do Guetto, the crew @djmarfox founded in 2005 with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo, and Príncipe Discos has since reissued it as a free download. His records went on to Enchufada, with Subliminar in 2013, and to Warp, whose 2015 Cargaa 1 EP had him at its centre.

Príncipe, Enchufada or the old eMule rips: where did you first hear batida? 👇

article.headline: From eMule to MoMA PS1: DJ Marfox and Lisbon's batida
article.standfirst: Born Marlon Silva in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe, DJ Marfox is credited with pioneering batida, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that came out of the city's housing estates. It fuses kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.
body: DJ Marfox, born Marlon Silva in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe, is best known for pioneering batida, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that came out of the city's housing estates. It fuses African-influenced dance music such as kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.

He has DJed as Marfox since 2002. The name joins "Marl" from Marlon with Star Fox, a Nintendo character he played as a teenager. In 2005 he founded DJs do Guetto with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo. A year later the crew put DJs do Ghetto Vol. I, a 37-track digital compilation, on eMule. Príncipe Discos has since reissued it as a free download, and it is seen as the founding release of the ghetto sound of Lisbon.

His first solo album, Eu sei quem Eu Sou (I Know Who I Am), came out on Príncipe Discos in early 2011. Philip Sherburne described it as "an atomic field of taut drums, hiccupping yelps, zapping synths and pinprick details." Artist Unknown (Pollinaire, 2012) and Subliminar (Enchufada, 2013) followed.

In 2014 his Lucky Punch EP on Lit City Trax made Dazed's top ten albums for August. He played Red Bull Music Academy in New York, and on 30 August he played MoMA PS1's Warm Up series. Rolling Stone also named him among its "10 New Artists You Need to Know" that year. Cedar Pasori wrote that the PS1 appearance "reinforced the accelerating spread of Afro-Portuguese dance music around the world."

On 13 March 2015 Warp announced the Cargaa 1 EP for 7 April, with Marfox as its central figure. Three days later Revolução 2005–2008, a collection of tracks he made in his bedroom in those years, came out on CD and as a free download. One of his first international collaborations was a rework of tUnE-yArDs' "Water Fountain" featuring the Brazilian band Pearls Negras. His Chapa Quente EP includes "Tarraxo Everyday".

points.text: In 2005 he founded DJs do Guetto with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo. Their 37-track DJs do Ghetto Vol. I went up on eMule in 2006 and is seen as the founding release of the Lisbon ghetto sound.

points.title: Taking it global
points.text: In 2014 came Red Bull Music Academy in New York, Rolling Stone's "10 New Artists You Need to Know" and MoMA PS1's Warm Up on 30 August. In spring 2015 Warp's Cargaa 1 EP put him at its centre.

article.headline: DJ Nigga Fox and Príncipe's disorienting polyrhythms
article.standfirst: Rogério Brandão Luís was born in Luanda in 1990 and moved to Lisbon at four. He made his first beats on a computer in his bedroom on the city's outskirts.
body: DJ Nigga Fox has taken the disorienting polyrhythms of Lisbon's Afro-Portuguese diaspora from Lux Frágil, Musicbox, Iminente and Porto's Hard Club to Berghain, Sónar, Club to Club, H0L0 in New York and WWW in Tokyo. Príncipe discovered him and started releasing his music in 2011. Since then Rogério Brandão Luís has become one of the leading artists to emerge from Portugal's Afro-descendant communities.

He was born in Luanda in 1990 to a Congolese mother and an Angolan father, and moved to Lisbon with his parents and older brother at four. He grew up on the outskirts of the city and started building beats and melodies on a computer in his bedroom.
His music starts from kuduro, afro house, tarraxinha and batida and pushes them into experimental polyrhythms. Pitchfork, The Wire and Trax Magazine have all recognised his work more than once.

Wider attention came in stages. In early 2015, when few people knew Príncipe or its releases, Thom Yorke of Radiohead shared a list of tracks he was listening to. It included "Weed" alongside producers like Kool A.D. and Bernard Parmegiani. In 2016, British filmmakers Tim & Barry premiered "Sons do Gueto", a documentary about Príncipe and the African-influenced electronic music made in Lisbon's suburbs and social housing estates. It presented him as one of the label's faces.

He has also worked in film. He contributed to the soundtracks of Pedro Costa's "Vitalina Varela" and Rita Maia and Vasco Viana's "Batida de Lisboa", and his music was part of the opening of Copenhagen's CPH:DOX festival in 2020.

His Warp Records debut came in 2014 with "LUMI" on the CARGAA 1 compilation, followed by Crânio in 2018. On Príncipe, his catalogue runs from O Meu Estilo EP (2013) through Noite E Dia (2015) and 15 Barras (2017) to Cartas Na Manga (2019).

points.title: The Yorke moment
points.text: In early 2015, when few people knew Príncipe or its releases, Thom Yorke of Radiohead shared tracks he was listening to. Among them was "Weed", on a list with producers like Kool A.D. and Bernard Parmegiani.

points.title: On screen
points.text: In 2016, British filmmakers Tim & Barry's documentary "Sons do Gueto" presented him as one of Príncipe's faces. In 2020, his soundtrack work for "Vitalina Varela" and "Batida de Lisboa" was part of CPH:DOX's opening.

points.text: O Meu Estilo EP (2013), Noite E Dia (2015), 15 Barras (2017) and Cartas Na Manga (2019) on Príncipe, plus Crânio (2018) on Warp Records.

article.headline: Branko: the Lisbon producer wiring up global club music
article.standfirst: Branko, the alias of Portuguese DJ and producer João Barbosa, built his 2015 debut album Atlas from travels around Cape Town, New York, Amsterdam and São Paulo. Princess Nokia, DJ Sliink and Rodes Rollins all appear on it.
body: Branko is the solo name of João Barbosa, a Portuguese DJ and producer born on 28 November 1980. His records connect club music from several continents, and his label and radio show are run out of Lisbon. He first became known as part of Buraka Som Sistema and previously went by J-Wow.

His debut album as Branko, Atlas, came out in 2015. It was inspired by his travels around Cape Town, New York, Amsterdam and São Paulo, and featured Princess Nokia and DJ Sliink, plus Rodes Rollins on "Out Of Sight (So Right)".

The network kept growing. "Let Me Go", with Mr. Carmack and Nonku Phiri, was picked up by i-D, Hypebeast and The Fader. Rolling Stone announced his second solo album, Nosso, on 22 January 2019. Its guests include Sango, Cosima, Mallu Magalhães, Dino d'Santiago, Catalina García of Monsieur Periné, Pierre Kwenders, Miles From Kinshasa, Umi Copper, PEDRO and Dengue Dengue Dengue. Outside his own releases, he worked with M.I.A. on her 2016 album AIM and has also worked with Santigold and Anik Khan.

Lisbon is the base for all of it. Branko hosts Enchufada Na Zona, a monthly show on NTS broadcast live from the Lisbon headquarters of the label Enchufada. The show inspired a compilation of the same name. In 2018 he was also one of the interval acts at the Eurovision Song Contest final in Lisbon.
His most recent chapter came in 2024, when he released the single "Slide" featuring Jay Prince, building up to the release of his album SOMA in March that year.

headline: Pete Tha Zouk: Locomia to DJ Mag's No. 37
caption:
Before DJ Mag's No. 37, @petethazouk learned the job watching the world's top DJs at Locomia.

When Chus heard his early track 'First Tribal Feeling', Pete went to Madrid to master it at the Chus & Ceballos studio. In 2003 he released 'Solid Textures' with DJ Vibe on Low Pressings, and in 2010 'Check This Out' came out on Sondos, Erick Morillo's label. In October 2011 he jumped from 81 to 37 in the DJ Mag Top 100, the highest any Portuguese DJ had ever placed.

Which Pete Tha Zouk track takes you straight back to a Portuguese dancefloor? 👇

article.headline: Pete Tha Zouk: Locomia to DJ Mag's No. 37
article.standfirst: On 20 October 2011, Pete Tha Zouk climbed 44 places in the DJ Mag Top 100, from 81 to 37. No Portuguese DJ had ever placed higher.
body: On 20 October 2011, Pete Tha Zouk was announced at number 37 in the DJ Mag Top 100. He had entered the chart at 81 the year before, so he climbed 44 places. It was the highest position a Portuguese DJ had ever reached.

His education came from the booth. António Pedro was born in Olhão in 1978 and started as a resident at two venues: Mitto, a bar that changed how the South starts its nights, and Locomia, the seafront club on Santa Eulália beach. All the world's best-known DJs played Locomia during the summer seasons, and Pete got to watch them work up close.

His first tracks, 'First Tribal Feeling' with Bruno Marciano and 'Kashmira', were big dancefloor hits in the early 2000s. 'First Tribal Feeling' caught the attention of Chus, and soon afterwards Pete was in Madrid mastering it at the Chus & Ceballos studio. 'Kashmira' and 'Enchantments' followed and made his name as a producer for the floor.

In 2003 he and DJ Vibe released 'Solid Textures' on Low Pressings. The track topped the charts, and at the 2004 Dance Club awards it won Single of the Year while Pete was named Best Producer. The same magazine had named him DJ Revelação in 2002.

In 2006 he joined the agency WDB, which took his career to Brazil, Switzerland and Angola. His first gig outside Portugal was New Year 2010/11 in Brazil. In 2010 he released 'Check This Out' on Sondos, Erick Morillo's label, and that same year made his DJ Mag Top 100 debut at 81.

points.title: The WDB years
points.text: He joined WDB in 2006 and became Portugal's most in-demand DJ. Promoters knew his name meant 'casa cheia', a full house. WDB then took him to Brazil, Switzerland and Angola.

points.title: The awards
points.text: In 2004 Dance Club named him Best Producer and gave 'Solid Textures' Single of the Year. He won Melhor DJ Português at the Prémios Noite.pt in 2005, 2006, 2008, 2009 and 2010.

points.title: Start here
points.text: 'First Tribal Feeling' (with Bruno Marciano), 'Kashmira', 'Solid Textures' (2003, with DJ Vibe, Low Pressings), 'Check This Out' (2010, Erick Morillo's Sondos), 'I'm Back Again' (2010, with Mastercris and Abigail Bailey).

headline: Hot Mix 5 founding member Kenny 'Jammin' Jason dies
caption:
"I miss you already… I'll tell this story if I'm alive to tell it." Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk

Kenny 'Jammin' Jason was a founding member of WBMX-FM's Hot Mix 5 (1981), whose radio mixes brought Chicago house to a wider audience. He also released the six-track 'Jam Tracks' EP in 1985 and made 'Can U Dance' with Fast Eddie. His death was announced on November 19th, and no cause has been disclosed.

article.headline: Hot Mix 5 founding member Kenny 'Jammin' Jason dies
article.standfirst: Kenny 'Jammin' Jason, the Chicago DJ, producer and remixer, has died. Fellow Hot Mix 5 member Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk announced his death on November 19th. No cause was given. Farley remembered him as his greatest musical mentor and a brother: "I miss you already… I'll tell this story if I'm alive to tell it."
body: Kenny 'Jammin' Jason, the Chicago DJ, producer, remixer and founding member of the Hot Mix 5, has died. Fellow Hot Mix 5 member Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk announced his death on November 19th, 2026. No cause of death has been disclosed.

In a tribute on Facebook, Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk remembered Jason as his greatest musical mentor and someone he considered a brother. "I miss you already," he wrote. "RIP. This really hits harder than anyone could know, and I'll tell this story if I'm alive to tell it."

Jason was one of the people who shaped Chicago's early house scene. He first made his name on local radio and at mobile disco parties, then joined the Hot Mix 5 on WBMX-FM. The collective was founded in 1981 by Jason, Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk, Mickey 'Mixin' Oliver, Ralphi Rosario and Scott 'Smokin' Silz, and its broadcasts introduced wider audiences to house music and the mixing techniques coming out of Chicago's clubs.

He also had a career as a producer and remixer. In 1985 he released 'Jam Tracks', a six-track instrumental EP. His production credits include work with Liz Torres and with Fast Eddie, with whom he made 'Can U Dance'. In 1986 he co-founded Hot Mix 5 Records with Oliver and Rosario, which gave music from the city's growing house scene another outlet.

Jason kept DJing in the decades that followed and stayed connected to Chicago radio and the local music community. DJ Kenny Jammin Jason Boulevard was named in recognition of his work, and in 2016 he reunited with his Hot Mix 5 colleagues for the collective's 35th-anniversary celebration.

points.title: The Hot Mix 5
points.text: Founded in 1981, the collective was Jason, Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk, Mickey 'Mixin' Oliver, Ralphi Rosario and Scott 'Smokin' Silz.

points.title: Studio credits
points.text: He released the six-track instrumental EP 'Jam Tracks' in 1985. His production credits include work with Liz Torres and 'Can U Dance' with Fast Eddie.

points.title: Hot Mix 5 Records & legacy
points.text: In 1986 he co-founded Hot Mix 5 Records with Oliver and Rosario. DJ Kenny Jammin Jason Boulevard is named after him, and in 2016 he reunited with the Hot Mix 5 for its 35th-anniversary celebration.

article.headline: Lilly Palmer played live from an ESA satellite chamber
article.standfirst: In 2023 Lilly Palmer, the German DJ and producer born Sonja Rauschenbach, played a live set from a satellite testing chamber at the European Space Agency, using samples from the ESA sound archive.
body: Lilly Palmer has played a live set from inside a satellite testing chamber at the European Space Agency. The 2023 performance incorporated samples from the ESA sound archive, and it is one of several unusual broadcasts in a career that took the German DJ and producer to No. 57 in the 2025 Top 100 DJs poll.

She was born Sonja Rauschenbach on April 5, 1989, and grew up in the Nuremberg area. Her career began in Zurich, where she worked in small bars and clubs playing mostly melodic techno and deep house. She later raised her tempo to 150 BPM because the crowd responded.

In June 2022 she recorded a two-hour, 28-track Essential Mix for BBC Radio 1. The ESA set came a year later. In 2024 she signed to Armada Music and Kontor Records, and "Hare Ram" was the first release under the deal. "My fantasy" and "Hype Boy" also came out that year.

In 2025 she played Sonus Festival and the Ushuaïa Ibiza Beach Hotel, then transmitted a live techno set from DJ Mag's headquarters. Her singles that year included "Late At Night" with Maddix and "Techy MF".
The press has taken note. Mixmag called her one of the "most exciting names in techno", DJ Mag called her a "star" and EDM.com named her one of its producers of the year in 2023.
In 2026 she released her album "Bigger Than Techno" and a double single with Armin van Buuren, "Ayi Giri" / "Dopamine Machine".

points.text: Zurich bars → BBC Radio 1 Essential Mix (2022) → ESA satellite testing chamber (2023) → Armada Music and Kontor Records (2024) → No. 57 in the Top 100 DJs poll (2025) → album Bigger Than Techno (2026).

points.title: What the press said
points.text: Mixmag called her one of the "most exciting names in techno", DJ Mag called her a "star" and EDM.com named her one of its 2023 producers of the year.

article.headline: Villalobos, Raresh, Magda: six days in Albania for €95
article.standfirst: UNUM Festival's Phase 1 for 2027 confirms more than 40 artists. Ricardo Villalobos, Raresh, Binh and Mathew Jonson lead it, with Dennis Cruz and Guti on the house side.
body: International early bird tickets for UNUM Festival 2027 are on sale for €95. The festival runs for six days and six nights, from June 3 to 8, on the Albanian coast. Its first lineup wave confirms more than 40 artists, led by Ricardo Villalobos, Raresh, Binh and Mathew Jonson.
Dennis Cruz and Guti cover the house side of Phase 1. Krystal Klear, Laidlaw, Cap, John Dimas and Priku are also booked, and the organisers say more names are coming.

Romania has a strong presence again. Raresh is joined by SIT (Cristi Cons & Vlad Caia), Arapu, DumitrEscu and Priku. The festival describes their sound as a deep dive into heady house and minimal and calls it an integral part of UNUM's spirit.

Several returning artists are on the list. Dana Ruh and Magda both played sets at earlier editions that the festival calls indelible. Alci, Anthea, Isaac Carter, Marlie, Rossko, Saraga and Traumer are also back.

UNUM bills itself as an independent festival for underground electronic music, with near-continuous music across three stages. The programme runs from extended daytime sessions through the night to sunrise, and guests can move freely between stages. According to the organisers, much of its international audience comes back year after year.
The €95 price is the international early bird rate and is sold through the festival's official website.

headline: SoundCloud can now claw back payouts from AI gamers
caption:
Weeks after signing AI deals, SoundCloud can now withhold or claw back payouts from users gaming it with AI.

The platform recently partnered with Moises and ElevenLabs, and now has terms that put payouts at risk for AI abuse. It's welcoming AI tools while drawing a line on how they're used, and it hasn't said publicly where exactly that line sits.

Producers: does this make you trust SoundCloud more, or worry your own uploads could get flagged? 👇

article.headline: SoundCloud can now claw back payouts from AI gamers
article.standfirst: A few weeks after it struck AI deals with Moises and ElevenLabs, SoundCloud has new terms aimed at users who use AI to game its systems.
body: SoundCloud has new terms that let it withhold, reverse or recover payouts from users who use AI to game its systems. The change comes only weeks after the platform struck AI deals with Moises and ElevenLabs.

That timing is the most interesting part of the story. SoundCloud is building partnerships with AI companies and, at nearly the same moment, setting rules against people who use AI to exploit the platform. The two moves don't cancel each other out. The terms aren't aimed at AI in general, only at using it to game SoundCloud's systems. But together they show the platform deciding which kinds of AI use it will accept.
Music Business Worldwide, which reported the change, describes it as a crackdown on “AI slop, spam, and excessive uploads”.

The penalty hits the money. Under the new terms, SoundCloud can hold back payouts, reverse them or recover them from users who use AI to game its systems. The report does not say how SoundCloud will spot that behaviour or what the threshold for action is.

SoundCloud is still a home base for many DJs and producers, for edits, mixes and early releases. For anyone earning money there, these new conditions on payouts are worth knowing about, especially while the rules on how they'll be enforced are still unclear.
